page: Amazon Web Services r8g.2xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 8 physical arm64 cores running at 2.8 GHz using AWS Neoverse-V2 processors, dedicated at one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. The hardware configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, backed by 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage, provides no discrete GPU hardware accelerators, and supports a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional memory subsystem capabilities. The PassMark memory test achieves a top 10% ranking at 3230.59 points, complemented by strong read-only large-block memory bandwidth of 189.8 GB/sec in the top 25%. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also registers in the upper quartile at 14.46 GB/sec. General CPU benchmarks sit within median expectations, with Geekbench yielding 1894.0 in single-core and 10117.0 in multi-core metrics, alongside 13638.32 on stress-ng multi-core testing. Tradeoffs appear in the PassMark encryption test and small-to-medium model LLM inference generation, both showing lower relative throughput.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers cost efficiency for operations limited by memory capacity and memory bandwidth rather than pure compute or floating-point acceleration. Dedicated core provisioning prevents contention across virtual threads, supporting predictable performance under concurrent load. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, distributed key-value stores such as Redis, enterprise caching tiers, search indices, and large-scale ETL data transformation workloads.
